record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: If X is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, must the bidual X^{**} contain an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace?

evidence.quote: Problem 15.1. If X is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, does X∗∗ contain an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $X^{**}$ denote its bidual (the continuous dual of the continuous dual $X^*$, equipped with its canonical norm). Recall that a Banach space $Y$ is reflexive if the canonical isometric embedding $Y \hookrightarrow Y^{**}$ is surjective; equivalently, the closed unit ball of $Y$ is weakly compact. Must $X^{**}$ contain a closed infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace?
artifact.status_search_result: A brief web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of the question whether the bidual of every infinite-dimensional Banach space must contain an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace. It is widely listed as an open problem in functional analysis problem collections, and no published solution was located in the search results.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorics in Banach space theory PROBLEMS
status_evidence.snippet: Problem lists in Banach space theory discuss reflexive subspace questions in biduals.
status_evidence.claim: The question concerning infinite-dimensional reflexive subspaces of biduals appears in problem collections without a known resolution.
